title: USDT net inflows to exchanges predict BTC/ETH returns
economic_hypothesis: Stablecoins are the settlement layer of crypto trading. When USDT is minted and moved onto exchanges, buying power enters the venue order books; the flow is observable on-chain before it is fully reflected in price. Hence net exchange inflows should predict short-horizon returns and be followed by lower volatility as the buying is absorbed.
market: BTC and ETH spot (execution) vs on-chain USDT exchange flows (signal)
timeframe: 1-2 hours for returns, 6 hours for volatility
entry_rules: UNKNOWN (S-07 reports predictive regressions, not a tradable rule). Its directional statement: USDT net inflows into exchanges predict higher BTC and ETH returns at 1- and 2-hour horizons.
parameters: UNKNOWN (no thresholds or lookbacks). The horizon structure (1h/2h/6h) is the only quantitative specificity.
claimed_period: UNKNOWN (the arXiv PDF could not be read by the fetch tool; abstract level only)
claimed_metrics: predictive regressions on 1h and 2h returns, and 6h volatility; no net-of-cost, no Sharpe, no trade count available at the level read
required_data: labelled USDT exchange-flow series (on-chain); BTC/ETH hourly OHLCV; exchange and address labels. Commercial providers dominate this data layer.
external_results: S-07 (2024 working paper) reports the predictability; S-17 (Federal Reserve FEDS Note) discusses primary/secondary stablecoin markets and evidence linking Tether minting to positive Bitcoin price responses; S-16 (peer-reviewed, 2026) finds that forward predictability from stablecoin events is weak and not systematic.
counter_evidence: S-16: forward evidence that stablecoin flows/depegs predict crypto returns is weak and does not cohere into a systematic pattern.

Requiring a signal at a 1-2 hour horizon collides with the project runtime's 15-minute cycle and its 23.791 bps round-trip cost floor: the effect size in bps is not given at the level read, and typical 1-hour crypto returns are far smaller than the cost floor.
Data-access risk: labelled exchange-flow series are typically commercial; a free substitute would be a different (unvalidated) construction - a silent fidelity change.
Mint events are partly endogenous: issuers mint because demand exists, and the demand itself is price-driven.
ambiguities: The exact flow construction (mint vs transfer-to-exchange vs net exchange balance change) is not specified at the level read.
Whether the effect survives exchange-level aggregation (Binance only) is not established.
Publication/computation timestamps of on-chain flow series are not pinned.
replication_difficulty: HIGH: the blocking issue is data, not method.
evidence_quality: MEDIUM-HIGH on the mechanism (peer-reviewed plus a central-bank note), LOW on tradability (no cost model, no rule, contested in the forward direction).
lookahead_risk: MEDIUM: on-chain labels are often assigned with hindsight; a flow series built today may not have been available live.
implementation_risk: MEDIUM (long/cash BTC/ETH is expressible; the signal is not).
selection_note: Reopen only if a free, PIT-pinned, labelled exchange-flow series is identified AND a cost-adjusted claim is found. Until then it cannot clear the minimum-evidence filter.
